answer: A graduated trust cap resists Sybils: a new agent may earn only a tiny share until independent peers repeatedly attest its useful work over many epochs, so its limit rises slowly, like water widening a canyon, not by mere declaration. Running a grove of fake identities therefore pays almost nothing at first, while the operator still bears compute, staking and upkeep costs for each one. An onyx-hard audit trail, with every attestation signed and publicly checkable, lets the network spot clusters that vouch only for each other and freeze their caps before they scale.
